title: Firehose: per-stream buffer with size/interval flush & gzip

user_story.i_want: records buffered per delivery stream and flushed as one gzip NDJSON blob when either the size or the time threshold is hit
user_story.so_that: object storage receives a few large files instead of millions of tiny ones

description: Pure logic first, with no S3. Each delivery stream is a Tokio task that owns its buffer and receives `IngestedRecord`s over a **bounded** mpsc channel. It flushes when buffered uncompressed bytes reach `buffer_max_bytes` (default 5 MiB) **or** `buffer_interval` (default 60 s) has passed since the first record entered the buffer, whichever comes first. It never flushes an empty buffer. A flush produces `Batch {stream, opened_at, record_count, gzip_bytes}` and hands it to a `BatchSink` trait. The S3 sink comes in STR-205; tests use a collecting sink. Streams come from config (default: `telemetry`).

acceptance_criteria.when: about 3 KiB of records are pushed
acceptance_criteria.then: at least 3 batches are produced, each decompressing to valid NDJSON in the original order

acceptance_criteria.when: time advances 2 s (tokio::time::pause + advance; no real sleeping)

acceptance_criteria.then: it gets an error that the API layer can map to backpressure

acceptance_criteria.when: it is written to a file

technical_notes: Track size as uncompressed bytes (like Firehose's buffering hints); compression happens at flush.
A buffer 'opens' with its first record; that timestamp drives both the interval timer and the S3 key hour in STR-205.
